# 2 Clement — Chapter 1 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Clement 1
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. My friends, we need to regard Jesus Christ the way we regard God — as the one who will judge the living and the dead. We cannot afford to treat our salvation as a small thing.
2. Because when we treat him as insignificant, we end up expecting very little from him. And people who listen to his message as if it barely matters are making a serious mistake — and so are we.
3. We need to recognize what we were given and who gave it, where we were brought from and what Jesus Christ willingly went through on our behalf.
4. How can we repay him? What kind of return could possibly match what we received? How many holy gifts did we owe to him!
5. He brought us into the light. He called us his children, as a father would. He rescued us when we were dying.
6. What praise is adequate? We were spiritually crippled, bowing down to stones and wood, gold and silver and bronze — things human hands made. Our whole existence was nothing but death. We were wrapped in darkness, our vision clouded by fog — until he opened our eyes and, by his own will, stripped away the veil that covered us.
7. He took pity on us. He saw our terrible error and ruin, saw that we had no hope of rescue apart from him — and out of deep compassion, he saved us.
8. He called us into being when we did not exist. He willed us to come to life out of nothing.
